results.q: What did you build at IDFC?
results.answer: At IDFC FIRST Bank, I developed Go and Python microservices, implemented Kafka retry handling, and tuned SQL queries over 50M+ records. I also built a Go MCP server with the team to expose banking capabilities to AI agents and prototyped an LLM-based cheque extraction tool. Additionally, I set up service observability and demoed loan and asset lookup tools to business teams.

results.q: How much faster did your SQL work make the APIs?
results.answer: My SQL tuning work, which involved optimizing queries and indexes over 50 million records, cut API response times by 42%.
I did not win Cal Hacks overall. My team and I earned 2nd place in the Claude for Public Benefit track at Cal Hacks 13.0 for our project, Drigil.

Drigil is a hackathon prototype I built with a three-person team at Cal Hacks 13.0. It uses smart glasses to coach people with intellectual and developmental disabilities through new jobs using their supervisor's voice. We earned 2nd place in Anthropic's Claude for Public Benefit track for this project.

results.q: What was your part in Mend?
results.answer: I built the pricing and rewards engine for Mend. This included surge pricing over H3 hexagons, the reward rate card, itemized receipts, bounty budgets, and pay-per-visit sponsored campaigns.
Mend was a finalist in the Top 15 teams at the USC Origin Hackathon 2026. It was not a winner.
